classification.difficultyReason: Factor a cubic to locate its zeros and compare reflected and vertically dilated curves.

content.prompt:
Let $f(x)=x^3-3x^2+2x$.

Sketch the graphs of $y=f(x)$, $y=-f(x)$ and $y=-2f(x)$ on the one set of axes.

answer.short:
All three curves cross the $x$-axis at $x=0,1,2$.

Reflect $y=f(x)$ in the $x$-axis for $y=-f(x)$; then stretch vertically by factor $2$ for $y=-2f(x)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=x(x^2-3x+2)\\f(x)&=x(x-1)(x-2)\end{align*}$$
Sketch a positive-leading cubic crossing the axis at $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$ and $(2,0)$.

Reflect this graph in the $x$-axis to obtain $y=-f(x)$. For $y=-2f(x)$, double every ordinate of the reflected graph. All three curves retain the same zeros; the last has twice the vertical distance from the axis as $y=-f(x)$.

spec.description: Three equation-driven cubic curves on shared axes with common zeros and distinct labelled series.
